questions.q: What should the sons not forget?
questions.a: The sons should not forget their father’s instruction.

questions.q: How did the father tell the son he would live?
questions.a: The father told the son he would live by keeping the father’s commands.

questions.q: What will Wisdom do for the son if the son does not forsake her, but loves her?
questions.a: Wisdom will watch over him and keep him safe.

questions.q: What will Wisdom do for the son if the son cherishes and embraces her?
questions.a: Wisdom will honor him, as if putting a crown of splendor on his head.

questions.q: In what way did the father teach the son?
questions.a: The father taught the son in the way of wisdom and directed him in how to live in the right way.

questions.q: On to what must the son grasp, for it is his life?
questions.a: The son must consistently remember the things his father has instructed him, for it is his life.

questions.q: What path must the son avoid?
questions.a: The son must avoid the path of the wicked ones.

questions.q: What do the wicked do before they can sleep?
questions.a: The wicked feel that they must do evil before they can sleep.

questions.q: What is the path of the righteous like?
questions.a: The path of the righteous is like the light of the sun that grows brighter until the brightest time of day.

questions.q: What is the way of the wicked like?
questions.a: The way of the wicked is like the darkness.

questions.q: Why must the son guard his heart extremely carefully?
questions.a: The son must guard his heart extremely carefully, for from it are the sources of life.

questions.q: What kind of speech and talk must the son put away?
questions.a: The son must put away speech that deceives or misleads people.

questions.q: Where must the son focus his gaze?
questions.a: The son must focus his gaze on doing what is right.

commentary.text: Exhortation to the study of wisdom.
Cautions against bad company, Exhortation to faith and holiness.

Verses 1–13 We must look upon our teachers as our fathers: though instruction carry in it reproof and correction, bid it welcome. Solomon's parents loved him, therefore taught him. Wise and godly men, in every age of the world, and rank in society, agree that true wisdom consists in obedience, and is united to happiness. Get wisdom, take pains for it. Get the rule over thy corruptions; take more pains to get this than the wealth of this world. An interest in Christ's salvation is necessary. This wisdom is the one thing needful. A soul without true wisdom and grace is a dead soul. How poor, contemptible, and wretched are those, who, with all their wealth and power, die without getting understanding, without Christ, without hope, and without God! Let us give heed to the sayings of Him who has the words of eternal life. Thus our path will be plain before us: by taking, and keeping fast hold of instruction, we shall avoid being straitened or stumbling.

The way of evil men may seem pleasant, and the nearest way to compass some end; but it is an evil way, and will end ill; if thou love thy God and thy soul, avoid it. It is not said, Keep at a due distance, but at a great distance; never think you can get far enough from it. The way of the righteous is light; Christ is their Way, and he is the Light. The saints will not be perfect till they reach heaven, but there they shall shine as the sun in his strength. The way of sin is as darkness. The way of the wicked is dark, therefore dangerous; they fall into sin, but know not how to avoid it. They fall into trouble, but never seek to know wherefore God contends with them, nor what will be in the end of it. This is the way we are bid to shun. Attentive hearing the word of God, is a good sign of a work of grace begun in the heart, and a good means of carrying it on. There is in the word of God a proper remedy for all diseases of the soul. Keep thy heart with all diligence. We must set a strict guard upon our souls; keep our hearts from doing hurt, and getting hurt. A good reason is given; because out of it are the issues of life. Above all, we should seek from the Lord Jesus that living water, the sanctifying Spirit, issuing forth unto everlasting life. Thus we shall be enabled to put away a froward mouth and perverse lips; our eyes will be turned from beholding vanity, looking straight forward, and walking by the rule of God's word, treading in the steps of our Lord and Master. Lord, forgive the past, and enable us to follow thee more closely for the time to come.
